faq_description: Clear explanations of the key things teams need to understand.
faq_accounts_question: Do employees need to create accounts?
faq_accounts_answer: No. A workplace can be open to anyone with the link or protected with a join code or private link. Access can be remembered on the device, which makes workhal practical on shared workplace computers and employees’ phones. An employee account is still recommended, though, because it lets managers assign roles and keep employee-specific data.
faq_difference_question: How is workhal different from Docs or Notion?
faq_difference_answer: Docs and Notion are flexible places to create pages. workhal is a ready-made employee portal: it starts with the workday, keeps published information separate from manager controls, connects guides to events and files, and gives staff one task-focused search across the workplace.
faq_content_answer: Use guides for repeatable tasks, the calendar for reservations, training, maintenance, and other operational dates, the document library for files and shared links, and common questions for fast everyday answers. Alongside these main features, workhal also includes smaller conveniences that make everyday work easier, such as personal notes for workers.
faq_maintainers_question: Can more than one person maintain the content?
faq_maintainers_answer: Yes. Give people view-only, editing, or full content access. Drafts stay out of the employee view until they are published, and the activity history shows who created, changed, or removed workplace content.
faq_gradual_question: Can we start without moving everything at once?
faq_gradual_answer: Yes. Start with the recurring answers, practical guides, and important dates the team needs most often, then add the rest at a pace the workplace can maintain.

about_page_title: Why this workplace portal exists - workhal
about_page_description: The thinking, firsthand problems, and personal story behind workhal—a workplace portal built to make useful knowledge easier to find and use.
about_title: A clearer way to pass work knowledge on.
about_intro: workhal started with a simple frustration: repetitive questions and important information scattered around.
about_story_title: A practical idea, shaped by real work.
about_story_paragraph_one: I’m the person behind workhal. While working in the service sector, I’ve encountered these issues myself. At first, I didn’t really think much of them, but as an employee, I felt bad about having to ask so many questions and repeat ones that had already been answered.
about_story_paragraph_two: At first, I thought that different tasks and procedures could be put into a convenient document, but then I looked further. It wasn’t just about tasks and questions; it was also about managing schedules, communication between managers and workers, and how general knowledge was passed on.
about_story_paragraph_three: I hope this application helps both managers and employees, and that my work makes someone’s day a little easier.
about_problems_title: The problems looked small. Together, they made every shift harder.
about_problems_description: workhal is a response to the everyday friction that turns simple tasks into repeated questions, avoidable interruptions, and work that is more complicated than it needs to be.
about_problem_one_description: A guide in one folder, an update in a chat, and the current answer in someone’s head. Finding the truth became work of its own.
about_problem_two_title: The right person became the search engine.
about_problem_two_description: The same dependable people were interrupted for the same answers, even when those answers had already been written down.
about_problem_three_title: Onboarding restarted with every new hire.
about_problem_three_description: Good training depended too much on who was working that day, leaving new people to piece together how things were really done.
about_principle: The goal is not more documentation. It is more confidence at work.
about_cta_description: Tell me how knowledge and onboarding work in your team. The best version of workhal will be shaped by those real conversations.

privacy_page_description: A simple explanation of how workhal handles details submitted through the contact form and beta waitlist.
privacy_intro: This policy covers the contact form and waitlist on this website. The workhal product is not connected to the site yet.
privacy_collect_body: For a general enquiry, workhal receives your name, email address, message, reason for getting in touch, and workplace name if you choose to provide it. If you join the waitlist, only your email address and selected reason are collected.
privacy_use_body: Information from general enquiries is only used to read and reply to your message. Resend and the receiving email provider process it to deliver the email. It is not sold to anyone.
privacy_waitlist_body: If you join the waitlist, your email address is used to record your interest and contact you about beta access and relevant workhal updates. You can ask to leave the waitlist at any time.
privacy_retention_body: General enquiry messages are kept only for as long as reasonably needed to answer and follow up. Waitlist email addresses are kept until you ask to be removed or the waitlist is no longer needed.
privacy_rights_body: You can ask what information is held about you, request a correction, ask for your message to be deleted, or leave the waitlist at any time.
privacy_contact_after: if you have a privacy question or want to make a request about your information.
